column7: MKII adds an A/B switch and a second Gain/Volume pair while retaining shared Tone controls; adds a 385+ high-gain switch; internally runs at 18V; manufacturer documents two enclosure/artwork treatments.
column10: The MKII is a clear example of a revision that materially changes the control surface and use case while preserving the 385 identity. Record enclosure artwork treatments separately from the core MKII generation.

column7: Channel 1 was completely redesigned for broader subtlety and warmer/deeper overdrive, with a clean Blend control; Channel 2 retains its British Plexi flavor. Top-mounted jacks and dual-channel architecture remain useful physical markers.
column10: Strong example where one channel changes while the other is documented as retained.

column7: V2 adds a 3-band EQ, bright and bass boosts, a Valve Screamer-style pre-gain boost usable while bypassed, and a side SAG switch. Vintage/Modern modes remain.
column10: External control changes provide strong identification markers.

column7: Manufacturer history distinguishes V1 large Ace Tone-inspired enclosure with front controls, V2 smaller pedalboard enclosure with top controls, and V3 larger enclosure with octave switching/expression and substantial octave-circuit refinement.
column10: Do not collapse V1/V2/V3 into one generic Life Pedal record.

column7: EarthQuaker publishes separate V1 and V2 manuals and current product documentation preserves both variant references. Core user interface remains the one-knob volume concept.
column10: Manual-version evidence should anchor variant mapping where exterior differences need further specimen research.

column7: Separate manufacturer V1 and V2 manuals exist. Current product documentation identifies the circuit as discrete, all-analog overdrive with a single More control.
column10: Do not imply a circuit revision solely from V2 labeling.
